title: Example 134: a window counter that advances by one window leaves its start behind a quiet client, found by a regression proof over the record results' shared components
description: Regression proof of net.terminalvalue.crosscut.ratelimit.Window#counted (a new fixed-window request counter kernel of Crosscut) across the counter record gaining a previousCount component: the old counter is built from the new components (--before-arguments 'new Window(this.startNanos, this.count), nowNanos, windowNanos') and the two record results are related on the components they share (--results-agree-when 'previous.startNanos == result.startNanos && previous.count == result.count'), within aligned starts as the scope. The new version advances the start by exactly one window instead of aligning it to the clock. Expected violation: a request two windows ahead of an empty counter, the old start at the request's window and the new one a window behind, found by JBMC in under a second inline.

resources.notes: the last run used a stale jvmcontract; measured by the submitting sessions in seconds at under 200 MiB, except 142 at bound 8, 7 s
